topic: Why the brain can reward you before a song's best part

sentences.text: Your brain can start rewarding you before a song's best part.
In scans of listeners, dopamine was released at peak emotional arousal.
The caudate was more involved during anticipation.
The nucleus accumbens was more involved at the peak.
Anticipation can use a pathway distinct from peak pleasure.

sources.title: Anatomically distinct dopamine release during anticipation and experience of peak emotion to music
sources.licence: abstract only, facts only, no text or figure reused

claims.claim: Music can arouse feelings of euphoria and craving, similar to tangible rewards that involve the striatal dopaminergic system.
claims.excerpt: Music, an abstract stimulus, can arouse feelings of euphoria and craving, similar to tangible rewards that involve the striatal dopaminergic system.

claims.claim: In listeners, endogenous dopamine release was found in the striatum at peak emotional arousal during music listening.
claims.excerpt: we found endogenous dopamine release in the striatum at peak emotional arousal during music listening.
claims.context: PET scanning with [11C]raclopride in human listeners. Release at peak arousal is a measured association.

claims.claim: In fMRI of the same listeners, the caudate was more involved during anticipation and the nucleus accumbens during the experience of peak emotional responses.
claims.excerpt: the caudate was more involved during the anticipation and the nucleus accumbens was more involved during the experience of peak emotional responses to music.
claims.context: fMRI with the same stimuli and listeners. 'More involved' is the abstract's wording; it is activity, not a dopamine measurement.

claims.claim: Anticipation of an abstract reward can result in dopamine release in an anatomical pathway distinct from the one associated with peak pleasure.
claims.excerpt: the anticipation of an abstract reward can result in dopamine release in an anatomical pathway distinct from that associated with the peak pleasure itself.
claims.context: One study. The abstract says 'can result in'; it does not say it always does.
